### Arteriosclerosis

Hyaline arteriolosclerosis: homogeneous pink hyaline in vessel walls, common in hypertension and diabetes. Hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis: concentric laminar smooth muscle proliferation (onion-skin) in malignant hypertension.

### Atherosclerosis

The most clinically significant form. Fatty streaks with foam cells may progress to fibrous-cap atheromas with lipid cores. Cholesterol clefts, calcification, and neovascularization characterize advanced plaques. Complications include ulceration, thrombosis, and aneurysm formation.

### Vasculitis

Giant Cell Arteritis: granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells at the internal elastic lamina. Polyarteritis Nodosa: segmental transmural fibrinoid necrosis in medium-sized arteries. Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (Wegener): necrotizing granulomas with vasculitis, crescentic glomerulonephritis, c-ANCA/PR3 positive. Kawasaki disease: childhood vasculitis with coronary artery aneurysm risk.

### Aneurysm and Dissection

Aortic aneurysm: medial degeneration with loss of smooth muscle and elastic fiber fragmentation. Aortic dissection: tear through the media creating a false lumen. Syphilitic aortitis: obliterative endarteritis of vasa vasorum with tree-bark appearance.

### Vascular Tumors

Hemangioma: most common benign vascular tumor. Kaposi Sarcoma: HHV-8-associated, spindle cells with slit-like vascular channels. Angiosarcoma: high-grade malignant vascular tumor with atypical endothelial cells.
